gap: No result ChatGPT got states that wireless CarPlay makes the iPhone hold open a Wi-Fi Direct channel and encode the screen in real time. Chigee calls this mirroring 'the single largest variable affecting power consumption', so a wire-free screen like the Aoocci F5 solves the screen's power but not the phone's, because the bike gives the phone no charging source.
standout_why: Of the results ChatGPT got, I opened motorcyclegpshub.com (best CarPlay/Android Auto list, dated 2026-11-11) and throttlebuff.com (7 best, dated 2026-11-04). motorcyclegpshub covers the 5 GHz Wi-Fi link, headset routing (paired to the phone vs. the screen's 'BT Trans' output) and the screen's 5 V/2.5 A USB supply. It says nothing about the phone's own battery drain. Throttlebuff only says the AIO-5 Lite 'Needs a power connection' and covers no battery-powered unit. ChatGPT's answer calls the F5 'self-powered' and doesn't say the phone still drains. I couldn't read the handlebarhq.com pages (TLS certificate error), so I can't rule them out.
decides: This tempers the pick rather than flipping it. The Aoocci F5's no-wiring pitch only covers the screen. On a bike with no USB outlet, the iPhone runs wireless CarPlay on its own battery, so for anything past short rides the shopper also needs a power bank or a handlebar charger. If they will wire a USB port for the phone anyway, a wired unit (Aoocci C3 at $105, Carpuride W702) can use the same supply, and the F5's $84 premium over the C3 buys little. One caveat: the drain explanation comes from Chigee, a rival brand, in its own blog. It gives no per-hour drain figure, and its fix is to sell a charging hub.

findings.label: Why wireless CarPlay drains the phone (maker's words)
findings.value: Wireless mirroring requires the phone to 'open a Wi-Fi Direct channel' and sustain real-time encoding; Chigee calls it 'the single largest variable affecting power consumption'
findings.source_title: Phone Battery Draining Fast with CarPlay on Your Motorcycle? 3 Real Causes and Fixes (CHIGEE, 2026-06-17)
findings.note: Chigee is a rival screen maker. The page gives no %/hour or watt figure; the 'full charge to 40%' example is a rider's report, not a Chigee measurement.

findings.label: Bluetooth headset draw and Wi-Fi/Bluetooth interference (maker's words)
findings.value: Bluetooth module 10–30 mA continuously with a headset connected and music playing; Wi-Fi and Bluetooth 'interfere with each other, causing packet retransmissions that push power consumption up on both sides'
findings.source_title: Phone Battery Draining Fast with CarPlay on Your Motorcycle? 3 Real Causes and Fixes (CHIGEE, 2026-06-17)
findings.note: Chigee also says a phone in a jacket pocket can exceed 45 °C surface temperature while navigating, and battery capacity shrinks at high temperature.

findings.label: Chigee's fix for long rides
findings.value: External charging for the phone: a separate power outlet or a handlebar charging mount (Chigee TR100 Charging Hub)
findings.source_title: Phone Battery Draining Fast with CarPlay on Your Motorcycle? 3 Real Causes and Fixes (CHIGEE, 2026-06-17)
findings.note: Chigee also notes its own display runs on the motorcycle battery. That is the opposite design from the battery-powered Aoocci F5.

findings.label: Screen USB supply needed (rival page already has this)
findings.value: Steady 5 V at 2.5 A (12.5 W) or more; Carpuride manual minimum 4.5 V at 2.5 A under load
findings.source_title: Best Motorcycle CarPlay & Android Auto Screens (2026), Motorcycle GPS Hub
findings.note: Included to show what the rivals already cover: power for the screen, not the phone.
